nearest_prs.skill: Load four items in a 0.6-scale washer; ordinary loading plus rotation check.
Put dropped basket wheels back on rail; basket realignment, not utensil extraction.
Reinstall two-part filter; weak relatability precedent acknowledged.
Load two cups and close upper rack; duplicate of RoboCasa LoadDishwasher.
Hang loaded caddy over wire rail by two hooks; no trapped utensil or appliance cavity.

physical_skill: Extract the actual unscaled tapered spatula through closely spaced rack wires inside a full-size countertop-appliance opening while managing an unconstrained wheeled basket; regrasp outside enclosure and restore free spray-arm rotation.
valid_shortcuts: One-arm recovery is allowed; bimanual motion is not a scoring requirement.
Rack may be pulled farther out or lifted if safely returned; no software guide locks it to the case. This still requires unthreading the utensil from the wire cage.
Pushing the rack home with the unrecovered utensil was physically tested; initialized recorded endpoint stalls the arm at 35.47 degrees under the same 1mNm test.
Setting the basket aside is permitted; ordinary utensil loading is not sufficient to undo the starting wire engagement.
Any extraction sequence that leaves the utensil released on the counter and rack home can score; no prescribed hand sequence.
distinct_from_nearest: RoboCasa LoadDishwasher and PR2221 are free-object placement followed by rack/door closure. This source starts with a real thin wooden handle threaded below the basket floor into the arm sweep. Clearance recovery, not changing dish arrangement, is the central manipulation. PR2385 is two-hook hanging on an exposed draining rack, not removal through a basket inside an enclosure. No pending/accepted counterpart was found in the refreshed board index; category acceptance still requires official review.
limitations: Internal wire/arm/rail dimensions are inferred from manufacturer photographs and declared; not manufacturer CAD.
Full-size countertop form is documented; no claim to a floor-standing dishwasher.
Novelty clearance is a reasoned assessment, not a guarantee of acceptance.

additional_benchmark_review.assessment: These test removal of interlocking puzzle pieces or a spiked ball from a cage. Clearance planning is a shared broad ability. This task requires recovery of an ordinary utensil from a free wheeled rack within a full-size appliance, followed by supported rack return; source mechanism and its valid alternatives were checked. Neither functional rotation testing nor a release requirement alone is claimed as the novelty. No exact task counterpart identified; broad skill overlap remains a review risk.
